Tomb of the Haterii.fact: The fragmentary titulus (founding inscription) names Quintus Haterius, of uncertain cognomen, and his wife Hateria as the founders of the tomb. The inscription indicates that at least Hateria was a former slave, and that Haterius was either a former slave of the same household or the former master of Hateria, who freed her in order to marry her.

Tomb of the Haterii.subject: Indian Architecture
Tomb of the Haterii.question: All four children's names are recorded with filiations, indicating that they were born free, and so after _____'s manumission
Tomb of the Haterii.fact: The titulus also dedicates the tomb to Quintus Haterius Rufio, either a close relative or former owner of Haterius and Hateria. A now-lost relief within the tomb gave Hateria the additional name of Helpis.

Tomb of the Haterii.subject: Indian Architecture
Tomb of the Haterii.question: Other inscriptions found in the tomb mention _____ and Hateria Supera, who died at the age of five
Tomb of the Haterii.fact: Other inscriptions found in the tomb mention Quintus Haterius Antigonus and Hateria Supera, who died at the age of five.

Tomb of the Haterii.subject: Indian Architecture
Tomb of the Haterii.question: The tomb is located approximately 8.4 kilometres (5.2 mi) south-east of Rome, along the route of the ancient _____ between the city and the town of Labici
Tomb of the Haterii.fact: The tomb is located approximately 8.4 kilometres (5.2 mi) south-east of Rome, along the route of the ancient Via Labicana between the city and the town of Labici.

Tomb of the Haterii.subject: Indian Architecture

Tomb of the Haterii.fact: The part of the lower storey excavated in 1970 consisted of a semi-interred burial chamber measuring 3.5 × 3.5 m. Tomb of the Haterii.fact: A hexastyle temple (with six columns) and with a pediment surmounted by an attic, dedicated to Jupiter. This may be either the Temple of Jupiter Tonans on the Capitoline Hill or the Temple of Jupiter Stator on the Palatine.

Tomb of the Haterii.subject: Indian Architecture

Tomb of the Haterii.subject: Indian Architecture

Tomb of the Haterii.question: A third relief, a funerary scene, is one of the few extant depictions of a collocatio (lying in repose) known from the _____ world
Tomb of the Haterii.fact: A third relief, a funerary scene, is one of the few extant depictions of a collocatio (lying in repose) known from the Roman world.

Tomb of the Haterii.subject: Indian Architecture
Tomb of the Haterii.question: The prominent position of women in the relief has been taken as evidence for "the predominance of women in mourning ritual" among the _____
Tomb of the Haterii.fact: The prominent position of women in the relief has been taken as evidence for "the predominance of women in mourning ritual" among the Romans. This motif is often found in sacred contexts, and has been taken as a reminder of the Rosalia, an annual festival from May to July in which Romans would dedicate their family's tombs with roses, and hold banquets in the tomb gardens.

Tomb of the Haterii.subject: Indian Architecture

Tomb of the Haterii.fact: Alongside the reliefs, two portraits inside a brick aedicula were found, along with an architrave with the busts of Mercury, Ceres, Proserpina and Pluto.

Tomb of the Haterii.subject: Indian Architecture

Tomb of the Haterii.subject: Indian Architecture

Tomb of the Haterii.fact: In particular, the collocatio relief is the only known example of its kind from Roman art, but follows precedents set up in Greek, Lucanian and Etruscan sculpture.
